title: SkinWorld Task Center
lastInspectedBy: Claude Code building the persona system for the needs section
sourceOfTruth: This file is the durable source of truth. Do not replace it with a new list; update tasks by stable id and retain completed items and history. Every task carries detectedIn, the lastInspectedAt value of the inspection that first registered it, which is what marks a finding as new. The rendered page is published as a Claude artifact at artifactUrl; always republish to that same url instead of creating a second Task Center.

statusDefinitions.pending: Open work that has been detected or accepted.
statusDefinitions.in_progress: Work has started but the completion criteria have not all been verified.
statusDefinitions.completed: The completion criteria were verified. Keep the task and its history.
statusDefinitions.requires_verification: A material production, operational, or owner confirmation is needed before classifying it as a defect or complete.

tasks.title: Make Stripe webhook failures retryable and observable
tasks.details: The webhook catches failures while reading or writing the order, logs them, and still returns HTTP 200. Stripe therefore treats the event as handled and does not retry it, which can leave a paid order absent from the administration panel.
tasks.doneWhen: A failed durable order write returns a retryable non-2xx response (or is reliably queued), duplicate deliveries remain idempotent, and a Stripe test event proves that a temporary database failure is retried and recorded with an actionable alert.

history.note: Detected in initial source audit.

Verified still open. The handler now short-circuits duplicate deliveries and a unique constraint on orders.stripe_session_id was confirmed live, so repeated events are safe; the catch block around the order write still logs and returns HTTP 200, so a database failure is still swallowed without a retry.

Fixed: the order write and the notification emails are now separate steps. A failure writing the order returns HTTP 500 so Stripe retries, and it also sends the shop an alert naming the Stripe session id so a charge without an order cannot pass unnoticed; a failing email only logs, because the order is already stored and a retry would duplicate the customer mail. Duplicate deliveries still short-circuit on the existing row, backed by the unique constraint on stripe_session_id verified live.

tasks.title: Decide and enforce inventory reservation and depletion
tasks.details: Checkout checks only the current in_stock flag. The inspected payment and webhook flow does not reserve inventory or decrement quantities. This is correct only if inventory is intentionally managed as a simple available/unavailable flag.
tasks.doneWhen: The owner confirms the inventory model. If quantities are required, payment completion atomically updates stock, overselling is prevented under concurrent checkout, and the admin shows the resulting stock state.

history.note: Needs business-rule confirmation; not asserted as a defect.

tasks.title: Add abuse protection to public write endpoints
tasks.details: The endpoints accept unauthenticated writes. Reviews have a honeypot and validation, but none of the three inspected routes applies rate limits, bot verification, or duplicate controls. They can be used to fill storage, create moderation noise, or trigger email notifications.
tasks.doneWhen: Rate limiting is enforced at an appropriate boundary; contact and newsletter writes have bot/duplicate protection; review moderation policy is implemented; and normal customer submissions still succeed.

history.note: Detected in initial source audit.

Fixed: contact, newsletter, reviews and the payment-status lookup now share an IP rate limiter (src/lib/limite.ts). Verified locally: three contact messages went through and the fourth returned 429; a filled honeypot returned 200 without storing anything (3 objects, not 4); the same address subscribed twice produced a single stored object, because the newsletter path is now derived from a hash of the email. Reviews get post-moderation: /admin/resenas lists them and deletes any that should not stay. The limiter lives in process memory, so on Vercel it is per instance — enough for repeated abuse from one address, and noted here rather than overstated.

tasks.title: Protect the admin login against repeated password attempts
tasks.details: The login route compares a single environment password and returns 401 on failure, with no throttling, lockout, or monitoring. The signed cookie has a browser expiry but its token itself contains no expiry or rotation data.
tasks.doneWhen: Failed attempts are rate-limited and logged without sensitive data, session revocation/expiry behavior is documented and tested, and the login flow remains usable for the administrator.

history.note: Detected in initial source audit.

Fixed: five failed attempts per IP in fifteen minutes, then 429; a correct password clears the counter so the owner is not locked out by their own typos. The comparison now runs over SHA-256 digests with timingSafeEqual instead of ===. Failed attempts are logged with the IP and never the password. Session expiry documented in the cookie (seven days). Verified locally: attempts one through five returned 401 and the sixth returned 429.

tasks.title: Harden checkout URL construction against untrusted request hosts
tasks.details: success_url, cancel_url, and local product image URLs are built from the incoming Origin or Host header. Use a configured canonical application URL or an allowlist instead of trusting request-controlled headers. Since the 2026-09-29 image fix, the same host-derived origin is also used to build the absolute product image URLs sent to Stripe, so a spoofed Host header now affects payment-page content as well as the success and cancel URLs.
tasks.doneWhen: Checkout URLs always use the approved production/preview application origin, unsupported hosts are rejected, and a checkout test confirms the correct return URLs and Stripe image URLs.

history.note: Detected in initial source audit.
Scope widened: the request-derived origin now also builds the product image URLs sent to Stripe.

Fixed: checkout URLs and the product image URLs sent to Stripe now come from src/lib/sitio.ts, which uses the canonical https://www.skinworld.shop and only honours the request origin when it is a localhost development address. A forged Host header can no longer redirect the buyer or place foreign images on the payment page.

tasks.title: Limit checkout-session data exposure
tasks.details: The unauthenticated session lookup returns a payment status, total, and customer email for any supplied Stripe Checkout Session ID. Session IDs are hard to guess, but the endpoint unnecessarily broadens the impact if one appears in logs, analytics, or a referrer.
tasks.doneWhen: The confirmation view receives only the minimum data it needs, with an authorization or one-time confirmation mechanism as appropriate, and no customer email is exposed by a reusable public endpoint.

history.note: Detected in initial source audit.

Fixed: /api/checkout/session no longer returns the customer email — only payment status and amount, which is all the confirmation page renders. The session id is validated against its expected shape and the endpoint is rate limited. The confirmation page now says the receipt was emailed instead of printing the address back.

tasks.title: Complete technical SEO metadata and discovery files
tasks.details: The root metadata has basic title and Open Graph text, but the audit found no robots.ts, sitemap.ts, metadataBase, canonical URL handling, Open Graph image, or product/blog-specific metadata generation. Confirmed by inspection: there is no src/app/sitemap.ts and no src/app/robots.ts, metadataBase is not set, and the canonical, author and Open Graph URLs point at https://skinworld.shop, which answers 308 and redirects to https://www.skinworld.shop — the domain actually served in production.
tasks.doneWhen: robots and sitemap are generated, canonical and social-preview URLs/images resolve correctly, and product/blog pages have accurate unique metadata validated in a production-like build.

history.note: Detected in initial source audit.
Added verified specifics: missing sitemap/robots routes, missing metadataBase, and apex-vs-www mismatch (apex returns 308 to www, confirmed with a live request).

Fixed: added src/app/robots.ts and src/app/sitemap.ts (176 URLs: 9 fixed pages, 164 products, 3 posts, revalidated hourly so catalog changes appear), set metadataBase and a title template on the root layout, and pointed every canonical, author and Open Graph URL at the www domain that production actually serves. Product, post, shop, blog, contact and about pages now emit their own title, description, canonical and Open Graph image. Verified against a production build and the running app: robots.txt and sitemap.xml return the expected content and the shop tab reads "Tienda · Skinworld".

tasks.title: Review legal copy for business accuracy and medical relevance
tasks.details: The terms describe a service about physical state and nutrition, which does not match a dermatology ecommerce site. Legal pages also need owner/legal review to confirm the responsible entity, address, providers, returns, delivery commitments, and effective dates. Specific gap confirmed in the privacy notice: the responsible party is given only as "Skinworld, con domicilio en la Ciudad de México", without the legal entity name (razón social), RFC or full address that the LFPDPPP requires.
tasks.doneWhen: A qualified owner or legal reviewer approves text tailored to SkinWorld, and all operational claims match the checkout, shipping, privacy, and provider configuration actually in use.

history.note: Detected wording mismatch plus legal facts requiring verification.
Recorded the concrete missing fields in the privacy notice: razón social, RFC and full legal domicile.
Unchanged and still blocked on the owner: completion needs the legal entity name, RFC and full domicile, plus a qualified reviewer. No code change can close this one.

Redesign re-audit found two additional operational mismatches: the terms still describe physical and nutritional status rather than dermatology ecommerce, and the shipping policy says the tracking number is sent with purchase confirmation even though the system can only send it after staff capture it when marking the order shipped.

tasks.title: Verify live payment, webhook, email, and order-fulfillment configuration
tasks.details: Live configuration must be confirmed against the real accounts rather than assumed. As of 2026-09-30 the Stripe webhook endpoint, the order write and the store notification email are verified working in production; what remains unconfirmed is the switch to live Stripe keys (tracked separately in SW-014) and customer-facing email delivery (tracked separately in SW-015).
tasks.doneWhen: A controlled production or staging purchase proves payment, order persistence, staff notification, customer confirmation, status-update emails, and cancellation behavior; deployment logs show the webhook arriving; and secrets remain server-only.

history.note: Marked requires verification; no credentials or live external state were inspected.

Partially verified in production: a real test purchase produced a stored order and the store notification email arrived. Remaining unknowns split into SW-014 (live payments) and SW-015 (customer email).

Redesign verification reached a correctly populated Stripe Checkout session from home, search, product, cart and postal-code address entry. It remains a test-mode session and no payment was completed, so webhook persistence and both email recipients were not re-verified in this pass.

tasks.title: Verify responsive and keyboard/screen-reader journeys
tasks.details: Manual browser checks now pass at desktop and 390 × 844 px: search and filter dialogs contain and restore focus, Escape closes them, mobile cards and product detail fit, cart controls have accessible names, and shipping labels are associated with their fields. A full screen-reader and automated accessibility scan is still outstanding.
tasks.doneWhen: The main buyer routes work at mobile and desktop breakpoints using keyboard only; focus is trapped/restored correctly in dialogs; form errors are announced; and an accessibility scan plus manual checks has no unresolved critical issue.

history.note: Browser/device testing was outside this source-only audit.

Advanced with browser evidence: desktop and 390px phone journeys were exercised through search, product, cart and checkout; dialog focus trapping and restoration passed. Shipping labels, postal-code status messages and remaining low-contrast checkout copy were fixed. Kept requires_verification until a screen-reader and automated scan are run.

tasks.title: Optimize image delivery and prevent failed product-image fallbacks
tasks.details: The storefront uses native img elements across product and editorial views. This works, but bypasses Next image sizing/optimization controls. The product-page fallback should also be tested with remote and local URLs. Confirmed by inspection: next/image is not imported anywhere — every image is a plain — so the images.remotePatterns entry in next.config.js is currently inert, and it only lists skinworld.mx while the catalog also serves images from frenchpharmacy.com, www.isdin.com and a lovelyskin.com CDN host plus 38 site-relative paths.
tasks.doneWhen: A performance measurement identifies the highest-impact images, correct dimensions/loading priority are applied, failed image URLs show an accessible fallback, and mobile Core Web Vitals improve or remain within targets.

history.note: Improvement, not a claim of current performance failure.
Added verified detail: zero next/image usage across the app; catalog images span four external hosts plus 38 local paths, none of them covered by the configured remotePatterns.

Partly done: created ImagenProducto, which replaces a failed image with a labelled "Imagen no disponible" block instead of a blank rectangle, and wired it into the product cards. Added lazy loading and async decoding to the shop, blog, about, search, brands and expertise images, and marked the images above the fold as eager. next.config.js now lists the four external image hosts the catalog really uses, so a future move to next/image will not drop those products. Still open, and the reason it stays open: no performance measurement has been taken, so the Core Web Vitals part of the completion criteria is unproven.

Redesign audit: 159 of the 201 product images are hot-linked from skinworld.mx, the old WordPress site. If that site is retired or its uploads move, those products lose their photo; copying the images into the project or Supabase Storage would remove that dependency.

tasks.title: Replace broad any types in payment and product paths
tasks.details: The production build passes, but several payment, product, and order values are typed as any. Stronger domain types and runtime schemas will reduce silent integration regressions.
tasks.doneWhen: Affected boundaries use explicit TypeScript types and input schemas; valid checkout, webhook, product, and admin flows continue passing type-check and integration tests.

history.note: Improvement derived from source audit; build currently passes.

Partly done: the Stripe webhook and the checkout route no longer use `any`. The webhook types the event and session as Stripe types, parses the shipping address through a new DireccionDeEnvio type, and guards the nullable amount and line-item fields; the checkout route validates cart items against an explicit shape and types its line items with Stripe.Checkout.SessionCreateParams.LineItem. Type-check and production build pass. Still open for the remaining `any` in the product detail client and the admin screens.

tasks.title: Verify all buyer-visible paths after catalog changes
tasks.details: The homepage is ISR-cached for one hour while catalog and product views use current server data. This has previously produced stale featured prices after a catalog update. The current source is configured with revalidate = 3600, but freshness must be checked whenever prices or featured products change.
tasks.doneWhen: After the next approved catalog change, homepage featured cards, catalog, product detail, cart, and hosted checkout all display the intended price and stock state after the documented cache window or an approved revalidation process.

history.note: Existing operational risk retained as a verification task; no present mismatch asserted.

Partial live evidence gathered: /api/codigo-postal returns correct data on production for CDMX, Michoacán, Oaxaca and Sonora, and a checkout session is created successfully from the live site. Full buyer-path verification after catalog changes is still outstanding.

The home page brand section is no longer a hand-written list: it is built from the catalog, so adding a laboratory in the panel now updates the front page by itself. Verified locally at desktop and phone widths, and each brand links to the shop already filtered — the SESDERMA link returns exactly the 31 products the home page promises.

tasks.title: Switch Stripe from test mode to live payments
tasks.details: Queried live on 2026-09-30: the configured Stripe key is a test key and the account reports charges_enabled=false and payouts_enabled=false. Real customers therefore cannot pay — the storefront takes orders only with Stripe test cards. Activating the account requires the owner to connect a bank account, after which the live secret and publishable keys must replace the test ones.
tasks.doneWhen: The Stripe account reports charges_enabled=true, live keys are set in Vercel, a live-mode webhook endpoint is registered for https://www.skinworld.shop/api/stripe/webhook with its own signing secret stored as STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and one real low-value purchase is completed, recorded and refunded.

history.note: Detected during the 2026-09-30 re-inspection.
Unchanged and still blocked on the owner: activating live payments requires connecting a bank account to the Stripe account, which only the owner can do.

Rechecked against the configured Stripe account: the keys are still test-mode and the account reports charges_enabled=false, payouts_enabled=false and details_submitted=false. The redesigned checkout reaches Stripe correctly, but only as an explicit test environment.

tasks.title: Confirm Resend domain verification and customer email delivery
tasks.details: RESEND_API_KEY and CONTACT_NOTIFY_EMAIL are set in Vercel and a store notification was received on 2026-09-29, so sending works — but it landed in spam because it was sent from the shared onboarding@resend.dev sender. The three Resend DNS records were confirmed present in public DNS on 2026-09-30 (TXT resend._domainkey plus CNAMEs rsend and send, both to forge.rmta.net), and the Hostinger MX and SPF records were confirmed unchanged. What is not confirmed is whether Resend marked the domain Verified and whether CONTACT_FROM_EMAIL was set; until both are true, Resend refuses mail to anyone other than the account owner, so order confirmations and packed/shipped notices never reach customers.
tasks.doneWhen: Resend shows skinworld.shop as Verified, CONTACT_FROM_EMAIL is set in Vercel, and a test sent from the admin panel to an outside address arrives in the inbox rather than spam.

history.note: Detected during the 2026-09-30 re-inspection.

The local environment used for redesign verification has none of RESEND_API_KEY, CONTACT_NOTIFY_EMAIL or CONTACT_FROM_EMAIL, so current production delivery could not be rechecked from this checkout. Code paths for store and customer mail exist; external inbox delivery remains unproven.

tasks.title: Stop rendering the shipping address form twice on the cart page
tasks.details: The cart renders <ShippingAddressForm /> twice — once in a lg:hidden block and once inside the desktop summary column — so both copies mount at every viewport and only CSS hides one. Each instance runs its own postal-code lookup effect, so every completed postal code fires two identical requests to /api/codigo-postal and both instances write to the shared store, and per-instance UI state such as the "write my own colonia" toggle can diverge between the two copies.
tasks.doneWhen: The form mounts once per page, a completed postal code triggers exactly one lookup request, and the layout still places it correctly on both mobile and desktop.

history.note: Detected during the 2026-09-30 re-inspection.

Fixed: the cart renders one ShippingAddressForm inside a single column that stacks under the products on mobile and sits in the sticky summary column on desktop. Verified in the browser: typing a postal code now produces exactly one GET /api/codigo-postal request, and the layout was checked at phone and 1400px widths.

tasks.title: Record tracking numbers and stage timestamps for orders
tasks.details: The orders table exposes only id, stripe_session_id, customer_email, customer_phone, shipping_name, shipping_address, amount_total, currency, status, items and created_at. There is nowhere to store a carrier tracking number, so the shipped notification cannot tell the customer how to follow the parcel, and there is no per-stage timestamp, so neither the panel nor the history shows when an order was packed or shipped. Adding these needs a schema change, which the service key used by the app cannot perform.
tasks.doneWhen: The orders table has columns for a tracking reference and stage timestamps, the admin panel captures the tracking number when marking an order shipped, and the shipped email includes it.

history.note: Detected during the 2026-09-30 re-inspection.

Blocked on a database change the application cannot make: the service key can read and write rows but not alter tables. The SQL is written and ready at supabase/migraciones/001-guia-y-mensajes.sql — it adds tracking, tracking_url and the packed/shipped/delivered timestamps. Once it is run in the Supabase SQL editor, the admin panel and the shipped email can be wired to it.

Fixed once the owner ran the migration. The orders table now has tracking, tracking_url and the packed/shipped/delivered timestamps. Marking an order shipped opens a field for the carrier number; the panel shows it, linking to the carrier when the number matches a recognisable FedEx, UPS or DHL format, and the shipped email carries it with a "Seguir el envío" link. Verified: the write persisted and was reverted, the rendered email contains the number and link, and the capture field was exercised in the panel.

tasks.title: Resolve the outstanding catalog decisions
tasks.details: The ISDIN Pediatrics stick and Daeha probiotic now appear in the catalog at $580 and $1,250 respectively, but this audit found no approval evidence for those prices. The Flavo C decision remains unresolved: only the generic "Flavo C Sérum 30 Ml" exists, without identifying Ultraglican, Melatonin, Forte, Intense or Día+Noche.
tasks.doneWhen: The owner confirms the Flavo C version and confirms the two already-published prices; the catalog then carries the approved IVA-inclusive values, names and images.

history.note: Detected during the 2026-09-30 re-inspection.

Redesign audit: the four products flagged as featured, shown on the home page as "Seleccionados por la Dra. Karina", are Effezel, Retacnyl, Clobexpro shampoo and Clobexpro lotion; three of the four have no brand, and they are prescription items. The planned "Skinworld Edit" section reads this same featured flag, so the owner should confirm the selection before it becomes the editorial centrepiece.
Current catalog check: Pediatrics Stick and Daeha are visible with prices, so the remaining work is owner approval of those values plus the exact Flavo C version.

tasks.title: Move contact and newsletter messages out of object storage
tasks.details: Contact messages and newsletter sign-ups are written as individual JSON objects in a private Supabase Storage bucket rather than a table, because the service key can create buckets but not tables. Reading the inbox downloads every object one by one, so the admin screen gets slower with each message and cannot search, sort or paginate.
tasks.doneWhen: Messages live in a table with an index on the date, the admin screen reads them in one query, and the existing stored objects have been migrated.

history.note: Detected during the 2026-09-30 re-inspection.

Blocked on the same database change: the messages table, its date index and the unique index per newsletter email are written at supabase/migraciones/001-guia-y-mensajes.sql. Meanwhile duplicate newsletter sign-ups no longer pile up, because the stored object is now keyed by a hash of the email, which removes the worst symptom while the table is pending.

Fixed once the owner ran the migration. Contact messages and newsletter sign-ups now live in the messages table, indexed by kind and date, and the admin screen reads them in one query instead of downloading every object. scripts/migrar-mensajes.mjs moves anything left in the old bucket and was run: zero objects remained. Verified: a contact message landed as a row, and the same address subscribed twice in different letter case produced a single row, because the unique index is case-insensitive.

tasks.title: Point the Stripe webhook at the domain actually served
tasks.details: The Stripe webhook endpoint was registered against https://skinworld.shop, but that apex domain answers 308 and redirects to https://www.skinworld.shop. Stripe does not follow redirects, so every checkout.session.completed delivery failed and no paid order was ever written to the database.
tasks.doneWhen: The registered endpoint points at the served domain and a real paid order is recorded automatically.

history.note: Detected during the 2026-09-30 re-inspection.

Fixed by repointing the endpoint to https://www.skinworld.shop/api/stripe/webhook and resending the pending event; the order appeared in the database immediately and a later real test purchase was recorded automatically. Verified against the Stripe API on 2026-09-30: endpoint enabled on the www host.

tasks.title: Accept checkout for products whose image is a site-relative path
tasks.details: Stripe rejects a checkout session whose line items carry a non-absolute image URL. 38 of the 201 catalog products store their image as a site path such as /images/productos/..., so a cart containing any one of them failed the whole payment with "Error al iniciar el pago".
tasks.doneWhen: A cart containing a product with a site-relative image reaches the Stripe payment page.

history.note: Detected during the 2026-09-30 re-inspection.
Fixed in commit 7768a24 by resolving site-relative paths against the request origin before sending them to Stripe. Verified on production: a cart with such a product returns a Stripe checkout URL.

tasks.title: Stop truncating the shipping address sent to Stripe
tasks.details: The whole shipping address travelled to Stripe as a single JSON string in one metadata key, and Stripe truncates any metadata value over 500 characters. A long but ordinary Mexican address measures around 494 characters, so a slightly longer one would have been cut, failed to parse in the webhook and been stored as an order with no delivery address.
tasks.doneWhen: Each address field travels in its own metadata key, the webhook still reads orders written in the old single-string format, and a long address survives the round trip intact.

history.note: Detected during the 2026-09-30 re-inspection.
Fixed in commit 51d4d03 by sending each field in its own metadata key, with the webhook still reading the previous format. Verified against the Stripe API: a long test address arrived complete.

tasks.title: Surface arriving orders on the admin home
tasks.details: The owner reported a paid order that "did not appear". The order was stored correctly and did show under the Pedidos screen, but /admin itself gave no sign that anything had arrived, so noticing a sale depended on remembering to open that screen.
tasks.doneWhen: The admin home shows how many orders still need attention and links straight to them, and the count drops as orders are marked shipped.

history.note: Detected during the 2026-09-30 re-inspection.

Fixed in commit f126fb8. The admin home now shows a pending-orders notice and a count on the Pedidos button, both rendered from a live query; confirmed by rendering the panel with the real order data.

tasks.title: Assign a brand to the products that have none
tasks.details: Counted on 2026-09-30: 46 of the 164 products the shop lists have an empty brand field — mostly prescription dermatology items such as Desowen, Nutracort, Presteme, Retacnyl and Bactroban. A customer filtering by brand never sees them, and they cannot appear in the brands section of the home page, which now builds itself from that same field. Roughly a quarter of the catalog is invisible to that whole way of browsing.
tasks.doneWhen: Every product either carries its laboratory in the brand field or is deliberately classified as having none, the shop brand filter accounts for all 164 products, and the home page brand list reflects the corrected data.

history.note: Found while rebuilding the brands section from the catalog: the section could only show 14 laboratories because the rest of the products carry no brand at all.
Recounted against the current catalog: the customer sees 164 grouped products and 46 still have no brand; the finding is unchanged.

tasks.title: Raise text contrast to WCAG AA across the storefront
tasks.details: Measured against white: body copy in text-slate-600 (#868E96) is 3.32:1 and 3.15:1 on the grey section background; text-slate-500 (#ADB5BD) is 2.07:1; text-slate-400 (#CED4DA), used for "Con IVA", category labels and dates, is 1.49:1. The small uppercase pink labels in primary-700 (#BC7F8F) are 3.2:1, the gold brand label gold-600 (#B8942A) is 2.87:1, and the About page call to action puts white text on primary-500 at 2.14:1. The project redefines Tailwind slate with much lighter values, so every default-looking grey class is lighter than it appears in code.
tasks.doneWhen: Body and small text reach at least 4.5:1 and large text at least 3:1 on their real backgrounds, verified with a contrast check of every text token in the new design system.

history.note: Found in the redesign audit by computing contrast ratios for every grey and pink text colour in use.

Fixed by the Skinworld V1 tokens: ink, body, muted and deep-pink text meet the documented ratios on their real surfaces. The remaining old low-contrast classes in the shipping and confirmation views were replaced, and both views were checked in the browser.

tasks.title: Reconcile the "free shipping in CDMX" promise with what checkout charges
tasks.details: The top bar, the closing call to action and the shipping page promise free shipping in CDMX. The checkout route charges a $100 shipping line to every order of $500 or less regardless of state, and the cart shows the same rule. A CDMX customer buying the $370 Cicaplast pays $470. Either the copy or the rule is wrong; which one is a business decision.
tasks.doneWhen: The owner states the real shipping policy, and the storefront copy and the checkout rule both match it.

history.note: Found in the redesign audit while tracing the cart summary back to /api/checkout. Not changed: the redesign will keep the current wording until the owner decides.

Reconfirmed in the redesigned flow: checkout still decides shipping only from subtotal and never reads the state, while four customer-facing locations promise free CDMX shipping. This remains a business decision, not a presentation fix.

tasks.title: Stop product cards from taking a full phone screen each
tasks.details: On a 390px phone the shop grid is one column and each card is about 1,000 CSS px tall (square image, category, name, price, "Con IVA", full-width black button), so the 164-product catalog is roughly 100 screens of scrolling. On the product page the square image fills the first screen and the price sits below the fold.
tasks.doneWhen: The phone catalog shows two products per row with a tappable add button, and the product page shows image, name and price within the first screen at 375-430px.

history.note: Measured from full-page captures of production on 2026-09-30.

Fixed and browser-verified at 390 × 844 px: the shop renders two cards per row with separate accessible add buttons, and the product image, name, price, quantity and add button all fit in the first phone screen.

tasks.title: Consolidate the butterfly and logo assets into one official version
tasks.details: The header and footer use a 512x407 PNG butterfly (the footer turns it white with a CSS filter). public/logo.svg is not the butterfly at all but a leaf drawing and is unused. public/images/logo-full.png has damaged transparency (speckled edges) and is unused. The butterfly pink measures #E9A9B9, while the site colour called primary is #D4A5AF, so the brand pink on the page does not match the logo.
tasks.doneWhen: One vector butterfly traced from the current header mark (same proportions) is used everywhere, unused or damaged logo files are retired, and the design system pink is taken from the logo.

history.note: Found in the redesign audit.

Fixed: header, footer, decorative marks and the new 3D motion use one vector component traced from the official butterfly; the design token uses its #E9A9B9 pink, and the unused damaged PNG and leaf SVG were removed.

tasks.title: Fix keyboard and semantic issues in product cards, menu and filter drawer
tasks.details: The product card places its "Agregar" button inside the product link, which nests two interactive controls. The mobile menu button does not expose aria-expanded. The mobile filter drawer has no Escape handling or focus management, and the mobile menu the same. Related to SW-010, which covers verifying the journeys on devices.
tasks.doneWhen: No interactive element is nested in another, menu and drawers announce their state, close with Escape and return focus, verified by keyboard.

history.note: Found by reading the components during the redesign audit.

Fixed and manually verified: product add buttons are outside the card links; menu and filter controls expose state; mobile menu, filter drawer and search close with Escape; filter and search dialogs contain and restore focus.

tasks.title: Visual redesign Skinworld V1 (presentation layer only)
tasks.details: Owner-requested redesign completed in nine phases: design system, global components, home, shop and cards, product page, About, Journal, contact and cart, followed by responsive, contrast and keyboard polish. Checkout logic, email behavior, APIs, database and admin remain governed by their own tasks.
tasks.doneWhen: Every phase is built, passes build and browser checks at 375-1920px, and the cart, filters, product add, forms and checkout still behave exactly as before.

history.note: Audit completed and plan presented; no files changed yet.

tasks.title: Produce the eight persona sequences for the needs section
tasks.details: The needs section shows one person per category, driven by scroll. The scene stays fixed on desktop, tablet and phone, and only the person moves: they enter from the left, turn on the vertical axis, improve during the turn and exit right, and the next person enters only after the previous one has left. The project has no photographs of people other than Dra. Karina, so no persona is shown yet and each category keeps its sculpture until its sequence exists. docs/personas-necesidades.md describes each condition as it really looks, based on dermatology sources and on what each category sells, with acne lesions only in Acné. It also holds eight different people, the asset specification and the generation prompts. scripts/preparar-persona.mjs turns a video or frame folder into optimised desktop and phone sequences and registers it. AI-generated skin-improvement imagery next to products may read as a result claim, so an "illustrative image" notice should be considered.
tasks.doneWhen: All eight sequences show a single person turning (never two heads), each a different person, with the condition shown as it really looks and an improvement that finishes before the end of the turn. All are registered in the manifest, and the owner approves them visually on desktop and phone before publishing.
